summary: This note covers the 1942–43 American Hockey League season, the league's seventh. Seven teams played 56 games each, and the New Haven Eagles folded 32 games into the season in January 1943. The Buffalo Bisons won the Western Division title (F. G. "Teddy" Oke Trophy) and their first Calder Cup as league champions.
one_line: Overview of the 1942–43 AHL season, when the Buffalo Bisons won the Western Division and their first Calder Cup.
key_facts: The 1942–43 AHL season was the seventh season of the American Hockey League.
Seven teams played 56 games each in the schedule.
An eighth team, the New Haven Eagles, ceased operations 32 games into the season.
The New Haven Eagles ceased operations in January 1943.
The Buffalo Bisons won the F. G. "Teddy" Oke Trophy as the Western Division champions.
The Buffalo Bisons won their first Calder Cup as league champions in the 1942–43 season.
